title: I gave a 2013 RPG (Shadowrun Returns) full voice acting as a solo modder: 3,900 lines, 126 characters, free on Nexus.
author: thewholeshelf
selftext:
Shadowrun Returns: Dead Man's Switch shipped with zero VO, \~420k characters of dialogue, and no voice mod in 13 years. It now has full voice acting: every conversation, a narrator for all 303 scene descriptions, voiced "Examine" interactions, and terminals with a robotic effect. Released free on Nexus, link at the bottom.

The voice generation itself (ElevenLabs v3) was the easy part. What made this shippable as one person was AI at every other stage:

* **Reverse engineering:** dialogue lives in protobuf `.convo.bytes` files inside a Unity 4 game. AI-assisted tooling decoded the schema, parsed the conversation trees, and attributed 3,253 NPC lines to their speakers.
* **Runtime injection:** a BepInEx plugin with a Harmony hook on the game's `ShowNodeText` plays an OGG keyed by conversation id + node index. Old Unity 4 Mono, so lots of "this API doesn't exist yet" archaeology.
* **Casting at scale:** I built a local web app to audition 180+ candidate voices per character with take history and keeper selection. Casting 126 characters by ear is only feasible when generating an audition is instant.
* **The part TTS alone can't do:** lines with engine variables like `$(l.name)` can't be spoken as written, and many lines interleave narrator prose with character speech in one text box. An LLM rewrote the variable lines in context and split the mixed lines into ordered narrator/character segments, so the spoken version flows while on-screen text stays untouched.
* **Direction:** generated at max expressiveness and regenerated bad takes instead of settling for the flat-but-safe setting. Every shipped take was human-reviewed.

Why I think this pattern matters: there's a huge back catalog of text-heavy games that will never get studio VO. This kind of mod is genuinely useful for players with reading fatigue or difficulties, and it's now a one-person project. For me this breathes potentially completely new life into a lot of old games.

Honest limitations: v3 occasionally misreads names, some lines took several regens (also to get the right tone etc.), and casting consistency still needs a human ear.

Mod: [https://www.nexusmods.com/shadowrunreturns/mods/282](https://www.nexusmods.com/shadowrunreturns/mods/282) (completely free)

Happy to go deeper on any stage of the pipeline in the comments.

comments.author: Tyalou
comments.body: Nice one! Impressive results, gives immediately a Disco Elysium vibe, which is the highest praise.

comments.body: Niice! Would be interesting to combine modern AI with the classic Infinite Engine, using image model to generate locations and the LLM to drive NPCs and DM.

comments.author: Unturned1
comments.body: Wow! How hard would it be to do Dragonfall following How you did it?

replies.author: thewholeshelf
replies.body:
I did the hard technical work, so quite easy. Now it's just a matter of curating and doing each character line by line. I'm actually slowly already in the process of doing it! I made a whole little application to make it easier for me.

https://preview.redd.it/jnx6dqol1tdh1.png?width=1910&format=png&auto=webp&s=687313cc200ac570b5272431b0169c4d70670109

replies.author: densewave
replies.body:
Have you thought of sharing your app? This is an interesting pipeline. Is the hardest part curating the text lines in a digestible way?

ElevenLabs api calls, human in the loop quality checks, programmatic progress management. I imagine the hardest part is setting up the project itself?

replies.author: thewholeshelf
replies.body:
I actually open sourced it: [https://github.com/MartinMouritzen/ShadowRun\_VoicePack](https://github.com/MartinMouritzen/ShadowRun_VoicePack)

So anyone can use it - I'd be more than happy if more people use it to create voice packs for games that didn't have any in the past!

comments.author: Melodic-Chemistry127
comments.body:
How much did it cost to generate all the lines? Have you explored any of the open models for these purposes?

Please do SR: HK next!

replies.author: thewholeshelf
replies.body:
I calculated that it cost about $60-80 for the first game and will be about $140 - $180 for each of the next two games (because they explode in dialogue)

I haven't explored the open models yet, because I've typically had best results with Elevenlabs - but I'll probably continue to refine the mods as voices and expressiveness becomes even better.

I will do the whole trilogy!

comments.author: zefenriden
comments.body: Well done. I'm really excited about this kind of use of AI. It suggests a lot of games can be more easily modded to be remastered or completely transformed.

comments.author: HebelKurier
comments.body: Did you use the Elevenlabs v3 model? From my experience, it is very expressive and natural but just not consistent at all from one generation to the next which makes it very frustrating for trying to retain one coherent voice. It will sound subtly different with every generation even with maximum stability.

replies.author: thewholeshelf
replies.body: Yep the elevenlabs v3 model with full creative instead of stability. I didn't feel I have much problems with the voice sounding that different, but sometimes I had to prompt several times and with a lot of \[tag\] guidance to get the right tone of voice.

comments.author: Muted-Koala1325
comments.body: This is complete genius, what a fantastic use of AI, might even win over some haters. You're gonna do the whole trilogy? You're my new hero 😁.

replies.author: thewholeshelf
replies.body: Thanks mate! Yes, I am 100% going to do the whole Trilogy and more games. It just takes a while - right now I'm still playing through Shadowrun Returns with different paths, to make sure I've actually listened to almost all lines in-game (it makes a big difference, compared to listening to them with the text in front of me, where I might not fully get the situation the character is in). And also capturing a few barks etc. that were not voiced in the first version. If nothing else, it's certainly a huge improvement for my own enjoyment 😄
